covers: US session of Monday 2 November 2026 (close and after-hours results) and overnight to 07:20 SAST Tuesday 3 November
headline: Breaking: Australia's central bank hikes to 4.85%, an 18-year high; Apple and Palantir beat but slip about 3% after hours; oil flat near $105 after a reported US strike on Iran's Qeshm Island
summary: On Wall Street on Monday the Dow rose 0.41% to 51,983.98 while the S&P 500 fell 0.51% to 7,541.40 and the Nasdaq 1.07% to 25,164.32, as technology dropped 2.66% and energy 3.97% on the oil slump (Xinhua, 3 Nov). After the close Apple and Palantir both beat estimates but fell about 3% after hours — Apple on a 45%–46% December-quarter gross margin guide hit by memory costs, Palantir on valuation worries (Investing.com, Yahoo Finance, 2 Nov). Brent settled 7.6% lower at $104.77 and was little changed near $104.80 early Tuesday after a WSJ report of US 'defensive' strikes on Qeshm Island, while Australia's central bank raised rates to 4.85%, the highest since 2008; gold held near $3,956 and the rand ended Monday near R16.62 ahead of the US midterms today and SA's local elections tomorrow (Business Recorder/Reuters, HDFC Sky, Domain, Investing.com, Trading Economics, 2–3 Nov).

items.title: Apple beats on revenue and profit but guides to a lower margin; shares down 2.8% after hours
items.summary: In John Ternus's first results as CEO, Apple's September-quarter revenue rose 12% to $114.5 billion and earnings per share 14% to $2.10 (Apple via MacRumors, 2 Nov), against forecasts of $113.38 billion and $1.99 (Investing.com, 2 Nov). iPhone sales rose 17% to $57.6 billion, Mac 24% to $10.8 billion, Services 10% to a record $31.6 billion and Greater China 21%; iPad fell 10% and Wearables 8% (MacRumors, 2 Nov). For the December quarter Apple expects revenue growth of 7%–10% and a gross margin of 45%–46%, with management blaming 'unprecedented' memory costs and Siri AI costs. The shares fell 2.8% to $328.85 after hours from a regular close of $338.32, itself down 1.83% (Investing.com, 2 Nov). LRC Stock Scanner: HOLD, score 60 (2 Nov) — rating unchanged.
items.source: Investing.com (call transcript), 2 Nov 2026; MacRumors, 2 Nov 2026; LRC Stock Scanner, 2 Nov 2026

items.title: Australia's central bank raises rates to 4.85%, the highest since 2008, in a split 6–3 vote
items.summary: The Reserve Bank of Australia raised its cash rate by 0.25 percentage points to 4.85% from 4.60% at 05:30 SAST on Tuesday, its fifth increase this year and the highest level since November 2008; six board members voted to raise and three to hold (Domain; investingLive, 3 Nov). The bank said inflation will stay above target for longer than forecast, partly because of higher global fuel prices linked to the Middle East conflict, and does not expect it back in its 2–3% band until late 2027 (Domain, 3 Nov). Governor Michele Bullock gave no guidance on the next move, and the Australian dollar eased after the widely expected decision (investingLive, 3 Nov). It is another sign that oil-driven inflation is keeping central banks cautious, which matters for the SARB's next steps and for the rand.

items.title: US reportedly strikes Iran's Qeshm Island; oil steadies near $105 after Monday's 7.6% fall
items.summary: The Wall Street Journal, citing US officials, reported that the US struck Iran's Qeshm Island in what officials called defensive strikes to stop attacks on commercial ships in the Strait of Hormuz (Reuters via Business Recorder, 3 Nov). At 01:04 GMT (03:04 SAST) on Tuesday Brent was up 0.5% at $105.25 and WTI up 0.5% at $96.93, after Brent settled down $8.66 (7.63%) at $104.77 on Monday on peace-talk hopes (Business Recorder, 3 Nov). The report has not been independently confirmed. By 06:04 SAST the gain had faded: Brent was up 0.03% at $104.80 and WTI up 0.18% at $96.63; Tehran said on Monday that contacts with Washington were continuing (HDFC Sky, 3 Nov). A renewed escalation would reverse part of Monday's relief for the rand and SA fuel prices.
items.source: Business Recorder (Reuters, citing WSJ), 3 Nov 2026; HDFC Sky, 3 Nov 2026

items.title: Palantir beats and raises full-year guidance to about 91% growth, but shares fall about 3% after hours
items.summary: Third-quarter revenue rose 96% to $2.3 billion against $2.18 billion expected, and adjusted EPS was 44 cents against 41 cents expected. US commercial revenue rose 148% to $984 million and US government revenue 96% to $953 million. Palantir guided fourth-quarter revenue to $2.64–$2.65 billion (analysts about $2.46 billion) and raised its 2026 revenue guide to $8.53 billion, about 91% growth (Fortune, 2 Nov). Shares rose about 1.5% at first, then fell about 3% after hours on valuation concerns (Fortune; Yahoo Finance, 2 Nov). LRC Stock Scanner: HOLD, score 70 (2 Nov) — rating unchanged.
items.source: Fortune, 2 Nov 2026; Yahoo Finance, 2 Nov 2026; LRC Stock Scanner, 2 Nov 2026

items.title: Dow up 0.4%, Nasdaq down 1.1% as tech sells off and energy falls with oil
items.summary: On Monday 2 November the Dow rose 213.67 points (0.41%) to 51,983.98, the S&P 500 fell 38.67 points (0.51%) to 7,541.40 and the Nasdaq fell 272.68 points (1.07%) to 25,164.32. Seven of 11 S&P sectors rose, led by consumer discretionary (+2.25%) and materials (+1.83%); energy fell 3.97% and technology 2.66%. Sherwin-Williams rose nearly 6% and Home Depot 3.6%. The S&P Global US manufacturing PMI was revised down to 54.9 for October from 56 (Xinhua, 3 Nov). Oracle fell 8.76% after its $20 billion stock-and-bond raise and Nvidia 1.26% (StockTitan, 2 Nov).

items.title: Futures little changed before the midterms; AMD reports after the close tonight
items.summary: At 18:47 New York time on Monday (01:47 SAST) S&P 500 futures were up 0.1%, Nasdaq-100 futures up 0.3% and Dow futures up 24 points (StockTitan, 2 Nov). The US midterm elections are today, Tuesday 3 November, with results due overnight into SA's Wednesday holiday. AMD reports after the US close tonight; Qualcomm and Arm on Wednesday; the October jobs report is on Friday 6 November at 15:30 SAST (TradingKey, 2 Nov).

items.title: Rand ends Monday near R16.62 after the AGOA announcement; local elections and a public holiday on Wednesday
items.summary: The rand closed Monday at R16.6225 per dollar, 0.51% firmer on the day, helped by a weaker dollar, firmer precious metals and lower oil, but still close to its weakest since late July (Trading Economics, 2 Nov). The US said on Monday that South Africa will lose AGOA duty-free access from 1 January 2027; AGOA preferential exports were about $1.7 billion, roughly 10% of SA's shipments to the US (SA People, 2 Nov). Wednesday 4 November is a public holiday for the local government elections, so the JSE trades today and then on Thursday.
items.source: Trading Economics, 2 Nov 2026; SA People, 2 Nov 2026

items.title: JSE gold and PGM miners bounce 3–6% on Monday; Sasol falls 5.6% with oil
items.summary: On Monday 2 November Gold Fields rose 5.9% to R585.50, Implats 4.5% to R171.20, Harmony 4.1% to R255.70, AngloGold Ashanti 3.9% to R1,392 and Sibanye-Stillwater 3.3% to R36.96, recovering part of Friday's 5.6%–6.4% falls, while Sasol fell 5.6% to R273.20 as oil slumped (LRC Stock Scanner, 2 Nov 2026).

items.title: Gold holds near $3,956 after its biggest daily gain in two months
items.summary: Spot gold was up 0.3% at $3,956.32 an ounce in Asian trade after rising 1.9% on Monday, when Iran's president said his government had more authority to pursue peace talks; US gold futures were 0.1% lower at $3,966.17. Silver rose 0.2% to $50.77, platinum 0.6% to $1,455.25 and palladium 0.6% to $973.37, and the dollar index eased to 101.80. Gold fell 6.8% in October (Investing.com, 2–3 Nov).

items.title: Brent $105.25 early Tuesday after a $8.66 fall on Monday
items.summary: Brent settled at $104.77 on Monday, down 7.63%, and traded at $105.25 (+0.5%) at 03:04 SAST Tuesday; WTI was at $96.93 (+0.5%) (Reuters via Business Recorder, 3 Nov). See Breaking for the Qeshm Island report.

items.title: Lumentum closes 18.6% lower and Marvell 12.7% lower after their $115 billion all-stock deal
items.summary: Lumentum fell 18.59% to $684.40 and Marvell 12.72% to $171.41 on Monday (StockTitan, 2 Nov) after Marvell agreed to buy Lumentum for 4.5 Marvell shares per Lumentum share (Marvell press release, 2 Nov). Because the price is fixed in Marvell shares, Marvell's fall cuts the deal's value to Lumentum holders. LRC Stock Scanner (2 Nov): Lumentum HOLD, score 52; Marvell HOLD, score 59, with a short-side trigger level of $206.50 — ratings unchanged.
items.source: StockTitan, 2 Nov 2026; LRC Stock Scanner, 2 Nov 2026

items.title: Apple (HOLD) and Palantir (HOLD) results: beats, but both lower after hours
items.summary: Apple fell 2.8% to $328.85 after hours on its margin guide; Palantir fell about 3% despite raising guidance (Investing.com; Yahoo Finance, 2 Nov). Details in Breaking. Ratings unchanged.

items.title: Oracle down 8.8% after its $20 billion raise; AMD reports tonight
items.summary: Oracle fell 8.76% on Monday after filing to raise $10 billion in stock and $10 billion in notes (StockTitan, 2 Nov). AMD (LRC Stock Scanner HOLD, score 65, 2 Nov) reports third-quarter results after the US close tonight (TradingKey, 2 Nov). Ratings unchanged.
items.source: StockTitan, 2 Nov 2026; LRC Stock Scanner, 2 Nov 2026
